text: Total points convert to the Danish 7-point grade average using a table re-issued each year and published by 1 March for that summer's intake.
If you retook to improve a result that already qualified you, Denmark converts your original result, not the improved one. The letter at the bottom left of the diploma says which it is.

Any IB English satisfies the English requirement. English A1, A2 or B at HL, and English A1 or A2, A Literature or A Language and Literature at SL, all count as Danish English A; English B SL counts as English B. No IELTS or TOEFL is needed.
A small, concentrated set — most degrees are taught in Danish

Danish universities have no tradition of campus accommodation. Most students live in kollegier, often some distance from campus, or rent privately. Start months before you arrive and contact your institution the moment you are accepted — August and September are the worst possible time to arrive without a room.
The English-taught bachelor programmes listed on this site are almost all here. Most university bachelor programmes are still taught in Danish.
The overwhelming majority of professionsbachelor programmes are taught in Danish, which is the practical barrier rather than the entry requirements.

The architecture schools, design schools, art academies, conservatoires and the film school. Admission runs on portfolio or audition, and grades matter far less than at a university — this is the one part of the Danish system where the usual logic of this site inverts. Preparation means a body of work built over months, not a supplementary course.

Denmark is the default option for most IB students at a Danish gymnasium, and the one where the rules are knowable in advance. An IB Diploma of 24 points or more opens every programme in the country, provided you also hold the specific subjects each one names. The two things that actually decide your application are the official conversion tables and the language a programme is taught in — most Danish bachelor's degrees are taught in Danish, and the English-taught set is smaller than people expect.
The deadline is 12:00 noon on 15 March, not midnight, and it applies to every IB holder including those who took the IB in Denmark.
Most bachelor's degrees are taught in Danish and require Danish at A level. The English-taught set is concentrated in a handful of institutions.
The conversion from IB points to the Danish grade average is published, so you can work out where you stand before you apply.
